newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Eurobourses end mixed, dlr and stg stronger.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Eurobourses end mixed, dlr and stg stronger.

text.p: European stock markets closed decisive rally was undermined by an unsteady start on Wall Street.

On currency markets, the dollar climbed strongly in early trade as bargain-hunters helped it recapture some of the ground lost on Friday. But it lost a little towards the close, nudged down by Wall Street's stumble and nerves over the direction of German interest rates.

Sterling also rebounded from Friday's sharp fall but traders said any further advance would have its wings clipped because of concern about what the Bundesbank might do and British inflation data later this week.

London, Frankfurt and Paris stocks all tumbled by about one percent at the opening before regaining some composure. They had been shaken by New York's two percent fall on Friday, which spread fears that the bull run on both sides of the Atlantic was slowing.
London, helped by benign price data on Monday, struggled back into positive territory after starting 64.9 points down at 4,966.4 on the FTSE 100 index.
But the advance ran out of steam near the close when Wall Street slipped 0.25 percent into the minus column. London eventually closed at 5,031.9, up 0.6 points.

The broader market, however, powered to a five-month peak on a favourable outlook for British interest rates and sterling. The FTSE 250 index of second-tier stocks, heavily influenced by industrial companies, gained 21.1 points to 4,671.6, its strongest since March 18.

"I think the idea of interest rates being on hold for the time being is factored in and for us to go further now will be based on individual earnings reports," said Roger Monson, chief equity strategist at Daiwa Europe.

In Frankfurt, stocks opened with losses of about one percent but later recovered some ground. Floor trade ended down about 0.50 percent and the after-hours, computerised IBIS index slipped to close down 9.16 points or 0.21 percent at 4,333.15.
Paris stocks, after briefly regaining positive terrain, slipped back into the red as Wall Street turned negative.
Activity was light as traders geared up for a three-day holiday weekend starting Friday. "It's relatively calm, it's not a huge sell-off," equity salesman John Fordyce at Oddo said.

The dollar, meanwhile, weakened slightly after building up momentum against the mark and the yen during the day. But it succeeded in correcting some of Friday's fall when it plunged four pfennigs and more than four yen in sympathy with the decline in U.S. asset markets.
The U.S. currency held onto its gain of one pfennig at 1.8547 marks and half a yen to 115.80 yen near the European close.
Though Monday's performance represented a healthy bounce, the dollar's outlook was clouded by talk that the Bundesbank might increase its key repurchase rate from 3.00 percent.
But many analysts expect the German central bank to stay put at Tuesday's repo tender because a rise in interest rates would hurt the nascent economic recovery in Germany.

The summer holiday period has reduced the number of players active in the market and increased volatility. During Friday's sell-off four big players - two Swiss and two U.S. banks - dominated trading, dealers said.
"Nervousness will continue even though at this stage people are more inclined to be buyers than sellers," said Chris Furness, foreign exchange strategist at 4Cast Ltd in London.
The British pound rebounded three pfennigs to 2.9485 marks and was up two cents to $1.5898. Sterling has been badly hit by official signals that British interest rates had peaked for the time being.
"There was something of an over-reaction last week in a thin market," Stewart Newnham, International Economist at First Chicago, said.

Sterling reached an eight-year peak of 3.0878 marks last month, when most analysts felt it was overvalued. Traders said the market was sitting on its hands ahead of sensitive British data late this week

But some remained upbeat. Jeremy Hawkins, chief economist for Europe at Bank of America, said: The pound is pretty much at a bottom now. Over the next few months we could be looking at a move up towards three marks again."
CURRENCIES
The dollar was quoted around 1.8547 marks and 115.80 yen in late European trade, compared with 1.8453 and 115.12 on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT THE EUROPEAN CLOSE
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index ended up 0.6 points at 5,031.9.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index closed 21.02 points down at 4,333.13 in bourse floor trade.
PARIS - The CAC-40 index finished down 12.83 points at 2,983.44.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in the afternoon at $327.20 an ounce, up from Friday's London close of $325.05. Silver was at $4.44, up three cents.
